CRM.rationale: CRM presents a cautiously attractive profile anchored by genuine fundamental improvement and a meaningful valuation discount to its own history, tempered by cash flow concerns and a hostile macro backdrop. The business trajectory is solid: revenue growing QoQ ($9.44B → $9.83B → $10.24B), operating margin inflecting to 22.8% in Q2 FY2026, and EPS accelerating +23.3% QoQ to $1.96. The franchise is durable — 22% global CRM market share, 90% Fortune 500 penetration, high switching costs — and Agentforce is showing early traction at $800M ARR with 29K deals. Valuation has compressed meaningfully: PE diluted at 36.3x sits at the floor of its 12-month range (34.6x–61.1x), down from ~55x a year ago, while the business is simultaneously accelerating. The balance sheet is a fortress (D/E 0.144, $61.33B equity vs $8.44B debt). However, three factors cap conviction: (1) the Q2 OCF collapse to $740M from $6.48B is a significant yellow flag on cash conversion quality that cannot be resolved without more data; (2) the 2.8% earnings yield sits below the 4.34% 10-year Treasury, meaning the stock is not cheap relative to risk-free alternatives; and (3) the macro regime of rising rates, $99 oil, and elevated VIX structurally compresses high-multiple software. The upcoming Q1 FY2027 earnings (expected 12.5% revenue growth, fastest in 13 quarters) provides a near-term catalyst, though slowing profit growth from AI costs introduces risk. Score sits between neutral and mildly attractive — the fundamental improvement and valuation compression are real, but cash flow uncertainty and macro headwinds prevent a stronger conviction call.
